newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia-Thai authority confirms Suriya gas find.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia-Thai authority confirms Suriya gas find.

text.p: The Malaysia-Thailand Joint Authority said on Monday that it has confirmed gas finds over the offshore Suriya field in a joint development area (JDA) between the two countries.
In a statement, the authority said its contractors in Block A-18 have completed drilling and testing the Suriya-2 appraisal well on the Suriya Gas field.
The Suriya-2 well was spudded on July 20 this year and was drilled to a total depth of 8,315 feet.
The tests yielded a combined maximum gas flow rate of 56 million standard cubic feet per day plus 268 barrels per day of condensate, measured through a two-inch choke, the statement said.
The operator is Carigali-Triton Operating Co Sdn Bhd, a 50:50 joint venture between Malaysia's Petronas and Triton Oil Co of Thailand.
The Malaysia-Thailand Joint Authority is a statutory body given the exclusive rights to explore and exploit petroleum resources in the joint development area under an agreement in 1990.
